query: What learner needs and pain points appear in survey responses?

per_column.name: pain_points
per_column.rationale: The 'pain points' half of the concept is a constitutive aspect OF learner needs and pain points; its multi-valued categories (instructor_feedback, hands_on_lab_access, social_isolation, etc.) enumerate genuine parts of the concept.

per_column.name: learner_needs
per_column.rationale: The 'learner needs' half is the other constitutive aspect OF the concept; categories like teacher_support, interactive_content, peer_connection are aspects of the concept itself.

per_column.name: response_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Overall response sentiment (positive/negative/mixed) is an affective property of the response text, not a constitutive part of the needs-and-pain-points concept. It is a generic sentiment tag, not a facet.

per_column.name: pain_point_count
per_column.rationale: A count derived from pain_points is an aggregate/measure over an existing facet, not an independent aspect of the concept; it re-expresses information already in pain_points.

judge.rationale: The concept has two natural constitutive halves: needs and pain points, and both are directly captured as multi-valued faceted columns (pain_points, learner_needs), which cleanly and non-redundantly carve the concept into its two main aspects. Mutual exclusivity is high because needs and pain points are conceptually distinct, though some categories mirror each other (e.g., instructor_feedback pain vs teacher_support need), creating mild latent overlap. Exhaustiveness is fairly good—together they cover the concept's principal constitutive aspects across pedagogical, social, technical, and access dimensions—though within-facet subcategories are somewhat coarse. The two non-facet columns weaken instruction following: response_sentiment is an irrelevant affective property external to the concept, and pain_point_count is a derived restatement of pain_points rather than a distinct facet.
